We need number of carbonyl (C=O) groups in the sample's molecule. IR spectrum shows a peak at 1739 cm-1, typical carbonyl stretch. Need to determine if there are multiple carbonyls. Only one carbonyl stretch appears. Could be overlapping but only one strong peak. So answer likely 1.

We could also check carbon NMR for carbonyl carbons (~190-210 ppm). But IR already indicates one carbonyl. To be safe, maybe use carbon NMR to see number of carbonyl carbons. Let's get carbon NMR.
